SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. __________
Special Branch ____ 8016
REPORT
Date ____ July ____ 20 ____ 1937

Subject ____ C.I. Znamensky, applicant for a position in the S.M.Police
(Special Branch).

Made by. ____ and ____ Forwarded by. ____ C.D.I. Ross

In accordance with the instructions of D. C. (Special
Branch) Mr. C.I. Znamensky, the writer of the attached letter,
was interviewed at Headquarters on July 12. At first he claimed
to be able to speak English, French and German with an equal
fluency and besides, to have a knowledge of the Japanese and
Chinese languages. However, it at once became evident that his
English is very poor and he had to speak through an interpreter.
As regards his knowledge of other languages he stated that owing
to absence of any practice for a long time, he had forgotten them.

When asked what special qualifications he had for
the work in the political section he was unable to give a clear
statement of his alleged vast experience in this line of work and
only reiterated what he said in his letter, namely, that for
13 years he had been connected with various organs of White
Russian Military Intelligence and Counter-espionage service in
Siberia, Maritime Province and Manchuria.

Upon being asked to give the names of the local
staff of the Soviet Consulate, he replied that he was not
interested in them.

Znamensky states that he was born in 1895 at
Petrograd. Upon graduating from a commercial school at Yamburg
(Petrograd District) he studied mathematics and physics at the
University of Petrograd from 1912 to 1916 and at the same time
followed a course in metallurgy at the Polytechnic Institute in
the same city. In 1915 he joined the army as a volunteer
and in August of the same year was sent to a military school for
officers in Irkutsk, Siberia. Upon graduating from this
establishment in 1916 he served in the army until April, 1917,
when he went to Harbin. Here he remained until 1918 when he

制作人：____ 转呈人：____ 首席副督察罗斯 (C.D.I. Ross)

遵照特别处副总巡 (D.C.) 的指示，附信作者 C.I. Znamensky 先生于 7 月 12 日在总部接受了面谈。起初他声称自己能同样流利地使用英语、法语和德语，此外还懂日语和汉语。然而，情况很快便表明他的英语非常糟糕，不得不通过翻译进行交流。至于他对其他语言的掌握情况，他表示由于长期缺乏练习，已经遗忘。

当被问及他在政治部门工作有何特殊资格时，他无法清晰陈述其自称在该领域拥有的丰富经验，只是重复了他在信中所说的话，即他在过去的 13 年里曾与西伯利亚、滨海省和满洲的各种白俄军事情报及反间谍机构有联系。

当被要求提供苏联领事馆当地职员的姓名时，他回答说他对这些人不感兴趣。

Znamensky 声称他于 1895 年出生在彼得格勒。从扬堡（彼得格勒区）的一所商业学校毕业后，他于 1912 年至 1916 年在彼得格勒大学学习数学和物理，同时在该市的理工学院修读冶金学课程。1915 年，他以志愿兵身份入伍，同年 8 月被派往西伯利亚伊尔库茨克的军官军校。1916 年从该校毕业后，他在军队服役至 1917 年 4 月，随后前往哈尔滨。他在此停留至 1918 年，当时他

    During the civil war in Siberia he was attached to the
Military Intelligence Department at Omsk and from 1919 to 1920
he served with Ataman Semenov's army at Chita. Following the
defeat of that army by the "reds" in December, 1920, he went to
Harbin.    During 1921-1922 he served in the White Forces in
Vladivostock where he was first attached to the Military Intelli-
gence and Counter-espionage Service and later to a technical
unit of that army. Following the evacuation of the Maritime
Province by the "Whites" in November, 1922, he went to Manchuria
via Genzan and subsequently resided in Harbin where he worked as
a teacher of mathematics. He also claims to have done political
intelligence work on behalf of General Gondatti in Harbin from
1922 to 1933. What the nature of this work was he was unable or
unwilling to explain satisfactorily.
    He left the Russian Imperial Army with the rank of
Lieutenant. Admiral Kolchak promoted him to the rank of Captain
in 1919 and he was made Lieutenant Colonel by Atamen Semenoff in
1920.
    Enquiries show that Znamensky arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin in March, 1934. Here he was without any fixed employment
and lived in very straightened circumstances until 1935 when he
was engaged as a teacher of drawing by the St. Jeanne d'Arc
College, 18 Route Doumer. He also resides, together with his
wife and three children, at this address.
    It appears that in 1933-1934 he made a trip to Japan
where he endeavoured to sell an alleged mechanical invention of
his, but without success. In Shanghai he is reported to have
made unsuccessful attempts to interest the Japanese and American

    在西伯利亚内战期间，他隶属于鄂木斯克的军事情报局，1919 年至 1920 年间，他在赤塔为谢苗诺夫 (Ataman Semenov) 将军的军队服役。1920 年 12 月该军队被“红军”击败后，他前往哈尔滨。1921-1922 年间，他在海参崴的白军部队服役，起初隶属于军事情报和反间谍部门，后来隶属于该军队的技术单位。1922 年 11 月白军撤离滨海省后，他经元山 (Genzan) 前往满洲，随后定居哈尔滨，担任数学教师。他还声称在 1922 年至 1933 年期间在哈尔滨为贡达蒂 (General Gondatti) 将军从事政治情报工作。对于这项工作的性质，他无法或不愿做出令人满意的解释。
    他离开俄罗斯帝国军队时的军衔是中尉。1919 年，高尔察克 (Admiral Kolchak) 海军上将将他晋升为上尉，1920 年谢苗诺夫 (Atamen Semenoff) 将他晋升为中校。
    调查显示，Znamensky 于 1934 年 3 月从哈尔滨抵达上海。在此期间，他没有固定职业，生活十分拮据，直到 1935 年他被杜美路 (Route Doumer) 18 号的圣贞德女中 (St. Jeanne d'Arc College) 聘为绘画教师。他与妻子及三个孩子也居住在此地址。
    据悉，1933-1934 年间他曾前往日本，试图出售一项据称是他发明的机械装置，但未获成功。据报道，他在上海也曾试图引起日本和美国

Shanghai,
5th July 1937.

Confidentially, Private.

To Commissioner
of Municipal Police Force, Esq.
Shanghai.

8016
20 7 37

Dear Sir,

By present my letter, I have the honour
to beg you very humbly to admit me to service
in the Political section, if it is possible.
I am Mr. C. J. Znamensky, 40 years old. My
parents was a Swedes, but I was born in Russia
and now I am Russian emigrant. I have
the higher education. I am ex-lieutenant
Colonel of the Russian engineering forces.
In the course of thirteen years I was
like Assistant Chief and after that like
Chief of the secret political search (opposide
Bolshevics and communists). I inquire (inform
myself) very well about the actual activity
all Russian societies and individual persons
among emigrants and bolshevics as in China
and Manchuria (now Manchu-ko) as in Japan.
All above - named can be confirmed
by documents.
I have the very excellent documents,

上海，
1937年7月5日。

机密，私人。

致
上海公共租界警务处总监 先生
上海。

8016
20 7 37

尊敬的先生：

谨以此信，卑职恳请阁下，如蒙允准，录用卑职在政治科服务。
卑职姓名为 C. J. Znamensky，现年 40 岁。卑职父母均为瑞典人，但卑职出生于俄罗斯，现为俄罗斯流亡者。卑职受过高等教育。卑职系前俄罗斯工程兵部队中校。
在十三年间，卑职曾任助理主任，此后任秘密政治搜查（针对布尔什维克和共产主义者）主任。卑职对在中国和满洲（现为满洲国）以及日本的流亡者和布尔什维克中的所有俄罗斯社团和个人的实际活动了解甚详。
上述一切均可由文件证实。
卑职持有极优秀的文件，
